slides.title:
From Screen
to Stay
slides.subtitle: An AI-led, evidence-audited map of connected hospitality experiences.
slides.body: The in-room display is becoming an experience-orchestration layer connecting guest comfort, property operations, and ecosystem value.
slides.alt_text: HXG title slide introducing the thesis that the in-room display is becoming an experience-orchestration layer.

slides.title: The screen is already a consequential touchpoint.
slides.subtitle: J.D. Power · 2026 North America Hotel Guest Satisfaction Index Study
slides.body: Availability and use establish relevance—not causal satisfaction, loyalty, or revenue.
slides.alt_text: Three statistics from J.D. Power: 74 percent availability, 62 percent usage, and a 44,787-person sample.

slides.title: Six outcomes. One human center.
slides.alt_text: A six-spoke wheel places human experience at the center of feeling at home, in control, recognized, included, secure, and supported.

slides.title:
Value starts human.
Property value must be measured.

columns.heading: Human value
columns.body: Time saved · reduced effort · familiarity · comfort · accessibility · control · trust

columns.heading: Property value
columns.body: Ancillary contribution · remote support · energy efficiency · experience indicators

formulae: Ancillary contribution = occupied room nights × engagement × conversion × margin
Energy savings = baseline spend × controllable share × verified reduction
Support savings = remotely resolved incidents × avoided dispatch cost
slides.context: ENERGY STAR: about 6% of lodging operating costs are energy; heating and cooling account for almost 40% of electricity use. Current agency guidance—not new 2026 measurement.
slides.alt_text: Human value and property value are separated, with property-specific formulas for ancillary contribution, energy, and support savings.

slides.title: The screen succeeds through relationships—not specifications alone.
slides.context: Nearly $805B projected U.S. hotel guest spending in 2026 is economic context—not screen-attributable revenue.
slides.alt_text: Six stakeholder groups surround the connected display ecosystem, with their distinct value mechanisms and an economic-context caveat.

slides.title: Samsung is one reference case—not the owner of the research.
slides.body: Samsung documentation shows how display hardware, cloud management, casting, IoT, PMS-connected services, security controls and analytics can form one hybrid stack.
slides.limitations: Availability varies by model, region, language, channel, device, software and licensing. Capability evidence does not establish guest or financial outcomes.
slides.alt_text: A clearly labeled vendor-stated Samsung reference architecture with seven components and availability limitations.

slides.title: Confidence is part of the finding.

states.name: Direct fact
states.example: LYNK Cloud supports central device management.

states.name: Supported inference
states.example: Remote visibility may reduce some on-site interventions.

states.name: Modeled scenario
states.example: Avoided visits × local dispatch cost = potential savings.

slides.alt_text: Three evidence states—direct fact, supported inference, and modeled scenario—plus four major contradiction-audit findings.

slides.title:
Audit the chain.
Reuse the graph.
slides.body: Release 0.1.0 is an interactive Codex-assisted seed audit with disclosed human governance. The configured local pipeline uses manager-led specialist agents and Microsoft GraphRAG; deterministic Python owns validation, counts and exports.
slides.alt_text: Methodology slide lists eight research stages, generated release counts, the public explorer URL, and a QR code only after live verification.
